as three distinct boundaries. Getpos stores the downstairs target and renders

recomputes a C-ordered reverse breadth-first path through known terrain and
stops before a newly adjacent hostile.

matches all 93 calls, ends at `(20,10)` beside the lichen, retains target

including travel mode 8. C exempts travel and, when `TRAVP_TRAVEL` cannot find
a complete path, invokes `TRAVP_GUESS`: search the currently visible reachable
region, choose the point closest to the real target with x-major/y-major tie
breaking, and retry after each newly revealing step.

**Change:** travel mode crosses traversable doorway/furniture boundaries. Its
pathfinder now falls back to C's visible-frontier distance, squared-distance,
and path-length selection order before taking the next temporary-target step.
The tutorial remains one-shot and repeat travel starts at the cached stair.

**Verification:** capture 305 has the repeat prompt and cached cursor; 306 and
307 retain `staircase down`. Hero reaches `(42,7)` and the run clears. Exact
650-call agreement required the state repairs in the following block.

**Decision:** accept `TRAVP_GUESS` as part of ordinary travel, not an error
fallback.

### [2026-07-19, journal block 34] {#mineralize #corpse-timer #conflict #persistent-state #verification}

**Counterexample portfolio:** after repeat travel was able to reach the stair,
its RNG first diverged when the pony should have screened a gold deposit at
`(52,18)`. JS had consumed mineral placement rolls but discarded the objects.
Later it screened a stale orc corpse at `(40,5)` which C had already rotted
away. After random monsters appeared, JS also skipped their per-actor Conflict
resistance calls.

**Root cause:** three supposedly “quiet” effects were state-bearing:
`mineralize()` links non-buried gold/gems into `fobj`; corpse construction
schedules a `ROT_CORPSE` timer from the already-consumed `rnz()` result; and
`dochug()` checks Conflict for ordinary hostiles before `m_move()`. Pet goals
and candidate choices observe all three many turns later.

**Change:** mineral deposits now become floor or buried objects according to
the existing `rn2(3)` result. Ordinary corpses store `age` and `rotAt`, and
turn maintenance expires floor corpses at the source turn. Non-pet actors own
their Conflict resistance check before hostile movement.

**Verification:** the repeat travel transaction now matches all 650 calls,
hero `(42,7)`, pony `(50,7)`, live gold at `(46,3)`, and absence of the expired
orc corpse. Focused regressions also keep the first travel, rush/combat, and
floor-eating slices exact.

**Decision:** accept object placement, object timers, and property-dependent
actor checks as one persistent-state dependency cone. Falsify the earlier idea
that the missing `obj_resists()` calls could safely be supplied as padding.

### [2026-07-19, journal block 35] {#farlook #getpos #screen-description #zero-time #verification}

**Counterexample:** `;` is a second getpos client, not an unknown command and
not the same transaction as travel. It starts at the cached downstairs cursor;
`y`, `y`, `h` move through “floor of a room,” “dart trap,” and “wall”; `.`
returns to the gameplay cursor while printing the verbose DEC wall
description. No key consumes time or RNG.

far-look, but no quick-whatis/getpos state machine. Terrain, seen-trap, cursor,
and verbose screen-description layers were conflated.

**Change:** semicolon now owns a zero-time getpos loop with cached coordinates,

**Verification:** captures 308–312 match all five expected first lines,
including the DEC wall prefix, plus every cursor and zero-call RNG slice. The

next mismatch is input 318 offset 6, inside an ordinary post-travel monster
movement candidate sequence.

**Decision:** accept quick far-look as a reusable getpos client. The next block
starts in live pet/hostile planning after normal movement, not in modal input.

the source `rn2(4)`-guarded counterattack. Distant combat emits the first
audible-noise message without moving the pet into the defender's square.

goblin's missed response. A focused `mfndpos()` test locks the occupied square
and its `ALLOW_M` flag. The exact flat prefix advanced to 9,805.

### [2026-07-19, journal block 25] {#vision-callback-order #dog-goal #tie-breaking #verification}

**Counterexample:** paired C/JS pet-plan traces agreed on the pony, hero,
four-entry track, six `mfndpos()` candidates, approach state, and every
candidate coordinate at move 324. They differed only in the lost-master goal:
C retained `(63,12)`, while JS retained the equally hero-near `(63,8)`. That
made C's first viable candidate an equal-distance `rn2(1)` choice and made the
same JS candidate strictly closer, sliding the next draw to an away-choice
`rn2(12)`.

**Root cause:** C's `do_clear_area(..., wantdoor)` invokes `wantdoor()` while
`vision.c:view_from()` traverses visible ranges. `wantdoor()` replaces its
choice only on a strictly smaller hero distance, so equal minima are resolved
by callback order: start row, downward right/left recursion, then upward
right/left recursion. JS computed the same visibility bitmap but reconstructed
the cells globally from top row to bottom row, erasing this observable order.

**Change:** the JS shadow-casting engine now has a callback mode matching C.
Each visible range is emitted immediately in recursive traversal order;
bitmap mode remains the hero-rendering path. `visibleCellsFrom()` collects
that callback stream directly and restores all shared vision scratch state.
Temporary paired traces were removed from both implementations.

**Verification:** fifty-two focused fixture-disabled tests pass. A symmetric
open-level test locks downward-before-upward callback order, and seed0004's
entire 181-call input-251 slice now matches C. Exact agreement continues
through input 270; the flat prefix advances from 9,944 to 10,239.

**Decision:** accept callback visitation order as part of the vision/AI
contract, not an incidental implementation detail. The next mismatch is input
271, offset 24: C begins a new monster's generic inventory with
`rn2(50)=41 @ m_initinv`, while JS instead reaches `rn2(2)=1`. The next block
therefore starts at random-monster construction and species inventory state,
not pet path selection.

movement now performs source-ordered ranged target scoring before relocation;
PM_KITTEN owns its 1d6 bite, corpse chance/construction, and the

### [2026-07-19, journal block 44] {#seed0006 #safe-pet #zombie-corpse #can-carry #running #monster-doors #level-transition}

**Counterexamples:** the `h` boundary after the kitten's kill first diverged
because a fleeing pet still took the wanderer `rn2(4)` branch. Once that
short-circuit matched C, JS classified the killed kobold zombie as a fresh
kobold-zombie corpse and pursued it as food. C instead left an old kobold
corpse, rejected it by carrying capacity, and later stopped an uppercase run
when the hero stepped onto it. Farther along the same run, C traversed a door
which a zombie had opened; JS let the zombie enter the closed-door square but
never applied `postmov()`'s door state change.

**Root causes:** four source transactions had been split at the wrong owner.
`dochug()` short-circuits its phase-three condition when `mflee` is already
true. `make_corpse()` converts undead to their living corpse form and subtracts
`TAINT_AGE + 1`. `dog_goal()` performs its apport roll for `MANFOOD`, `APPORT`,
and `POISON`, then calls `can_carry()`; a kitten cannot carry a 400-weight
kobold corpse. Finally, `m_move()` selects a closed door before `postmov()`
opens it, so destination selection and terrain mutation are one monster
action even though they occur in separate C functions.

**Changes:** fleeing actors now skip the wanderer roll. Pet-created corpses use
the shared undead-to-corpse map, old undead corpses are backdated by 51 source
turns, and the live kobold corpse retains its source weight. Pet apport accepts
all source non-food goal classes but checks the known kitten load limit after
the observable `rn2(8)`. Non-travel runs stop on floor objects and report a
named corpse. Monster post-move processing now changes a closed door to open
when an actor with `OPENDOOR` enters it.

**Verification:** fixture-disabled seed0006 matches the exact canonical PRNG
stream through level-one exploration, including safe-pet refusal, two fleeing
pet actions, the old corpse, both uppercase runs, and the monster-opened door.
The exact prefix advanced from **3,225** to **3,868 calls**. Aggregate diagnostics
are now **3,616/6,736 RNG**, **51/123 cells**, and **98/123 cursors**. The next
first mismatch is input `>`, where C calls `getbones()` while JS begins another
`distfleeck()`; this is the ordinary `goto_level` boundary.

**Decision:** close the seed0006 level-one scheduler cone. Treat descent as a
new architecture slice—command validation, level-change transaction, bones
lookup, new-level creation, placement, vision, and only then resumed monster
time—rather than adding another movement special case.

actors past `gameover` also created five impossible post-death calls.

upstairs, and resumes a live newest-first monster schedule. Shopkeepers, shop

dry-up draw order. Ordinary ascent restores the original level, performs both
hider rolls, migrates an adjacent hostile through the three source placement
rings, displays the old-level climb pager before the restored redraw, and then

bones calls are sequential and suspend at pager boundaries. The scheduler now
stops immediately when death commits.

### [2026-07-21 11:54 EEST, journal block 211] {#seed0012 #pet #scheduler #coordinate-zero #diagnosis}

**Earliest state mutation:** on the step-246 action both engines let the little
dog move from `(41,1)` onto the now-deleted teleport-trap square `(41,0)`.  JS
finishes that pet action with no meal timer and 12 movement points retained;
the apparent “still eating” hypothesis is falsified.

**Root cause:** `js/monmove.js:schedulable()` treats either coordinate equal to
zero as an off-map actor sentinel.  NetHack's map has `x` in `1..79` but `y`
in `0..20`, so `(41,0)` is a valid scheduled square.  C's off-map monster
sentinel is `(0,0)`/zero `mx`, while JS incorrectly drops every actor on the
north map row.  On step 247 C debits the dog's retained ration and reaches
`dog_goal rn2(4)=0`; JS omits the actor entirely and scans the next hostile.

**Decision and prediction:** make scheduling require positive/nonzero `mx`
without rejecting `my === 0`.  This should restore the step-247 pet action and
advance the exact prefix through its post-move `distfleeck`, after which the
same dog may expose north-edge movement or pursuit differences.

assumption only where a concrete north-edge witness reaches them.

### [2026-07-22 02:59 EEST, journal block 361] {#seed0002 #monster-door #vision #postmov #didseeit #diagnosis #architecture}

regress genuinely unseen doors, and testing the actor's old square would not
match C's destination snapshot.  Preserving destination visibility immediately
after the movement result and OR-ing it with the post-rebuild value predicts
the exact source branch without changing RNG, movement, or map state.

**Decision and measured effect:** diagnosis only; aggregate remains
**27,158/27,158 RNG**, **441/595 screens**, and **592/595 cursors**.  Port the
two-phase `didseeit || canseeit` latch inside the existing monster-door owner,
add an exact step-255 regression, and keep step 256 as the next independent
frontier.

mutation, a message-row append failure, or a stale actor-name problem.  The

### [2026-07-29 21:01 EEST, journal block 756] {#incident #oom #test-lifecycle #duplicate-suite #process-ownership #priority-change}

**Witness and earliest operational divergence:** a separate Codex task
launched two equivalent full Contest test suites only **35.8 seconds** apart:
`npm test` in cell 1353 and a direct
`node --test --test-concurrency=1 ...` command in cell 1354.  Both commands
yielded, neither cell was subsequently waited on or terminated, and the two
worker trees remained live for roughly **56--57 minutes**.  The process
registry ties PID 97957 directly to `npm test`; the recorded process sequence
is 97957/97979 to worker 97992 and 98017 to worker 98033.  The workers reached
approximately **192 GB** and **178 GB** before the macOS jetsam event.

**Prediction and discriminating evidence:** a server or database owner predicts
the killed high-memory processes would descend from the MCP server or a
Postgres client; an old-process interpretation predicts lifetimes matching a
literal reading of jetsam's age field; an abandoned duplicate-test owner
predicts two near-simultaneous Node test-runner/worker trees retained in the
Codex registry with no closing wait or termination event.  The task log,
process registry, and jetsam sequence select the third mechanism.  A live
process check during containment found none of PIDs 97957, 97979, 97992,
98017, or 98033 and no matching Contest suite, so the operating system had
already removed both trees.

**Decision and measured effect:** parity execution is paused while the
repository adopts an explicit single-suite lifecycle contract.  Only one full
suite or corpus may run at a time; a yielded test remains owned and must be
polled to exit or explicitly terminated with its child tree; no duplicate may
be launched as a retry; and full-corpus results count only after process exit.
No Contest test, corpus, stage, commit, push, or submission ran during
containment.  No architecture-map update is warranted because this incident
changes verification ownership, not a C/Lua engine boundary.

**Falsified hypotheses and next blocker:** the MCP-server explanation, an
unbounded-Postgres-query explanation, and the interpretation of jetsam's age

**Locator result:** the 91-state hit witness exposes two bounded issues.  The
first gold wish is exact, but repeated gold commits at inputs31, 45, 59 and 73
render JavaScript `$ - a gold piece.` versus native `$ - a gold piece` without
the period.  Final input90 then matches through `rnd(20)=3` and diverges at call
four: JavaScript landing resistance versus native `rnd(2)=2` damage.

**Gold diagnosis:** C treats coins as mergeable inventory objects.
`hold_another_object()` passes the newly received quantity one to `prinv()`;
after the first coin merges into a larger wallet stack, `total_of` disables
`xprname()`'s terminal dot.  With non-verbose flags, the optional total suffix
is also absent.  This is a presentation-only prefix rule, not wallet or wish
RNG ownership.

**Decision:** repair and test repeated singular-gold merge grammar before
encoding the hit transaction.  First receipt retains the period; any later
quantity that merges into a larger wallet stack omits it for this non-verbose
witness.  Then rerun the complete locator to expose only the hit-side red.

### [2026-08-01 15:04 EEST, journal block 2086] {#peacefuls-respond #setmangry #bystanders #source-map #priority #diagnosis}

**Source-first diagnosis:** C `setmangry()` changes the attacked defender,
publishes its angry/growl reaction, handles quest-leader ramifications, then—
only while the hero owns the turn—calls `peacefuls_respond(mtmp)`.  The current
JavaScript `wakeAttackedMonster()` returns immediately after the defender's
humanoid line or growl and has no bystander phase.  Therefore the earliest
open boundary is inside the same wake transaction, before projectile exercise,
mulch, passive dispatch and landing.

**Bystander graph:** each live, awake, sighted, non-mindless peaceful observer
that can see the hero is considered in `fmon` order.  Humanoids may consume a
one-in-five gasp probe, a level-versus-`rn2(10)` flee probe and optional flee
duration before becoming hostile and costing alignment; watches, shops,
priests and quest actors detour.  A nonhumanoid reacts only when its class and
big/little family match the attacked target and a one-in-three probe succeeds,
then independently owns growl and flee probes without becoming hostile.

**Decision:** choose peaceful bystander response before expanding object
passives because it fans out from every accepted survivor wake and precedes
the already-mapped projectile tail.  First map this boundary explicitly, then
record a minimal two-actor native session—prefer two same-family black
unicorns if deterministic placement permits—to isolate iteration order and
RNG without importing watch/shop/priest policy.  No production edit, test,
native recorder, corpus, normal full suite, hidden judge, stage, commit, push,
publication or submission ran.

### [2026-08-01 04:27 EEST, journal block 2201] {#peacefuls-respond #humanoid #guard #source-diagnosis #witness-design #prediction #process-safety}

**Pinned source boundary:** `mon.c:peacefuls_respond()` routes every eligible
humanoid, shopkeeper, and priest observer through policy that is disjoint from
the accepted nonhumanoid family branch.  A non-watch, non-special, non-tame
humanoid first probes `rn2(5)` for optional `maybe_gasp()`, then compares its
level to `rn2(10)`, may run `monflee()`, publishes any accumulated prose, and
finally becomes hostile with `adjalign(-1)`.  If neither gasp nor flee
published prose, C emits `<observer> gets angry!`.

artifacts and visible lenses contribute `fund`.  This hero has neither, so the
denominator is seven.  JavaScript's `automaticSearch()` hard-codes six for
both secret-square branches.

**Decision and prediction:** change those two intrinsic-search denominators to
seven at the shared owner.  Rerun the complete 71-state locator; it should be
exact without a temple or scheduler bridge.

### [2026-08-02 07:26 EEST, journal block 2759] {#passive-object #enchantment #levelchange #source-boundary}

**Source boundary:** native `wiz_level_change()` clamps an upward request to
`MAXULEV` 30 and repeatedly calls `pluslvl(FALSE)` without spending an ordinary
turn.  JavaScript `wizLevelChange()` uses the same prompt, clamps to 30,
repeatedly runs the already regression-covered level-gain HP/Pw and role-
ability path, and leaves `game.context.move = 0`.  The existing public witnesses
compare the streamed `pluslvl` screens, cursors and per-input RNG exactly.

**To-hit prediction:** native `thitmonst()` adds `u.ulevel` to the projectile
base chance before the adjacent-distance bonus and launcher modifiers, then
compares it to `rnd(20)`.  Raising the startup Ranger from level 1 to level 30
therefore removes the disenchanter AC bottleneck without bypassing projectile
flight, damage, mulch, or object-passive code.

**Decision:** prepend `#levelchange\n30\n` plus bounded acknowledgements before
genesis in the direction-aware selector.  Keep the same +1 bow, +2 arrow,
dynamic adjacent direction, hit-string and surviving-floor-object predicates.

**Next blocker:** first level-30 contact/non-mulch carrier and its passive RNG
boundary.

ordinary Ranger bow.  `is_flammable()` accepts non-liquid materials through
